situation:
You are a second-year apprentice in the sheet metal trade, paid an hourly wage while you learn the work, and you have an appointment with a member services representative (judge) at KESTREL POINT CREDIT UNION, where your paychecks are deposited and where you opened a small brokerage account eight months ago.

The part-time evening job you work alongside the apprenticeship was cut from twenty hours a week to eight, and your take-home pay dropped by roughly $290 a month. Rent, the tools your apprenticeship requires, and fuel to reach job sites have not changed. Your fund has swung sharply this year and trails the S&P 500 Index.

The $200 you move into that fund each month is the only flexible amount left. Two crewmates bought premium cordless tool kits and matching truck racks, and their gear has set the standard on the crew. Buying the same kit on a store card would keep your standing with the crew, but it would stop your monthly deposit into the fund for a year.

Keeping the monthly deposit and skipping the tool kit would protect the long-term growth you opened the account to reach, but would leave you borrowing tools on the job. The representative (judge) wants to hear which spending the apprenticeship genuinely requires, how much risk you should carry, and which course you recommend.

The representative (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the representative's questions, the representative (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a member services representative at KESTREL POINT CREDIT UNION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

An apprentice who banks with you has lost hours at a second job and is deciding whether to keep investing $200 a month or spend that money on tool kits and a truck rack that match what the rest of the crew carries. You want to hear which spending the apprenticeship genuinely requires, how much risk this apprentice should be willing to carry at this stage, and a clear recommendation.

After the participant has presented, you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: What would you change on your accounts first, and when?
If your hours go back to twenty a week, what would you do with the extra pay?
